morphology.shape: Ring, trophozoite, schizont, and gametocyte stages within red blood cells
morphology.size: Infected RBCs are typically enlarged with fine Schüffner's dots

protozoanDetails.lifeCycleForm: Ring, ameboid trophozoite, schizont, and gametocyte stages in blood; dormant hypnozoites in the liver responsible for relapse

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human liver (hepatic stage) and red blood cells (erythrocytic stage); Anopheles mosquito (sexual/sporogonic stage)
habitat.hostAssociation: Human-mosquito life cycle; preferentially invades reticulocytes (young red blood cells), limiting parasitemia compared to P. falciparum
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Widespread in tropical and subtropical regions, notably South/Southeast Asia and Latin America
habitat.reservoir: Infected humans; Anopheles mosquitoes as the vector

microscopy.stain: Giemsa-stained thick and thin blood smears
microscopy.appearance: Enlarged infected RBCs with fine Schüffner's dots; ameboid trophozoites; schizonts with 12-24 merozoites
microscopy.arrangement: Intraerythrocytic parasites at multiple developmental stages simultaneously

culture.growthCharacteristics: Obligate intracellular parasite with a complex human-mosquito life cycle

identificationClues: Giemsa-stained thick and thin blood smears remain the diagnostic gold standard
Enlarged infected RBCs with Schüffner's dots distinguish it from P. falciparum
Rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) detect Plasmodium antigens
Hypnozoite liver stage causes relapse months to years after initial infection

diseases: Relapsing malaria due to reactivation of dormant liver hypnozoites
clinicalImportance.transmission: Bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: The most geographically widespread cause of human malaria, especially prevalent in South and Southeast Asia and parts of Latin America; generally lower mortality than P. falciparum but a major cause of morbidity due to relapse
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Requires treatment with a hypnozoite-active agent (e.g. primaquine or tafenoquine, after G6PD testing) in addition to blood-stage therapy to prevent relapse

examFacts.importantTest: Giemsa-stained blood smear; rapid diagnostic antigen test
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Forms dormant hepatic hypnozoites responsible for relapse, unlike P. falciparum
